subject: RFI: TAM coverage windows, on-call notification protocol, and incident comms
messages:
From: Alan Reed <alan.reed@cedarbrook.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, procurement@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RFI - Support / TAM questions (Cedarbrook)

Mina --

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As part of Cedarbrook's platform procurement we attached a short set of questions focused on support coverage, TAM responsibilities, incident notification SLAs, and on-call escalation paths. Can you confirm Redwood's staffing model for TAMs, the 24/7 support coverage options, and what our teams should expect during a Sev1?

Key asks in the attached PDF:
- TAM assigned hours and overlap with Cedarbrook business hours
- On-call escalation flow and mean time to acknowledge/engage for Sev1/Sev2
- Notification channels (email, SMS, webhook) and who receives which notifications
- Playbook for incident comms (customer-facing templates, status page cadence)
- Evidence of SOC2 controls around incident logging and audit trails

We need a written response by COB Dec 3 to include in our vendor evaluation pack. Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Alan Reed
Head of Procurement, Cedarbrook Financial
alan.reed@cedarbrook.com
+1 415-555-0182

Attachment: Cedarbrook_RFI_Support_Questions.pdf (pdf, 2 pages)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-30T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: RFI - Support / TAM questions (Cedarbrook) -- need consolidated answers

Team -- forwarding Cedarbrook's PDF. They want a written response by COB Dec 3. Draft scope below, can each of you add specifics where relevant and I'll consolidate into a single doc and reply. Keep answers succinct; procurement will paste into their RFP template.

Proposed sections:
1) TAM staffing model + escalation responsibilities (Karthik)
2) Coverage windows (hours, SLAs for hosted vs dedicated) (Marcus)
3) Incident notification channels + sample webhook payload (Lauren)
4) SOC2 / audit evidence pointers (I'll attach our SOC2 summary)

Notes: we should not promise custom 24/7 TAM coverage without pricing/contract. We offer 24/7 support via our incident on-call and can provide optional TAM coverage windows (business hours + extended) as a paid add-on. Recommend we offer: 
- Standard TAM: 9am–5pm local support (M–F) with next-business-day roadmap meetings
- Enhanced TAM: 24/7 on-call liaison with guaranteed response within 60 minutes for Sev1 after engagement (contracted)

Please add bullets inline and return within EOD.

-Mina

-- Forwarded attachment: Cedarbrook_RFI_Support_Questions.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@redwood.com
Date: 2025-12-01T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI - Support / TAM questions (Cedarbrook)

Mina — adding TAM details below to paste into the RFI. Happy to join the call if Cedarbrook wants a technical run-through.

TAM staffing model and responsibilities:
- Primary TAM assigned per account; backed by a cross-functional support pod (platform SRE, infra ops, CS manager) for escalations.
- TAM responsibilities: onboarding and runbooks, weekly health checks, cadence for optimizations (cost & perf), playbook ownership for major incidents, liaison for security/compliance requests.
- Standard engagement: 9:00–17:00 local business hours (M–F) for proactive activities; incident coordination handled by support outside these hours via on-call.
- Enhanced engagement (contracted): dedicated TAM on-call rotation with overlap windows to customer business hours plus 4 hours of nightly coverage; guaranteed access to TAM within 60 minutes for Sev1 during contracted coverage.
- Handoffs: documented escalation matrix and SOC2-compliant logs for every incident; TAM performs post-incident RCA coordination.

I'll attach a simple table for the RFI in the consolidated reply (rows: offering, hours, response SLA, price band reference).

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@redwood.com
Date: 2025-12-01T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI - Support / TAM questions (Cedarbrook)

Mina / Karthik — adding incident notification and comms section (paste-ready):

Notification channels and escalation flow:
- Initial alerting: platform monitoring triggers routed to on-call SRE (PagerDuty) and to the customer notification webhook if configured.
- Customer channels supported: email, SMS, webhook (JSON payload), and optional Slack integration. We can send owner- and severity-tagged notifications.
- Acknowledge/Engage SLAs (standard):
  - Sev1: Support acknowledges within 30 minutes during business hours; engage engineering within 60 minutes. Outside business hours acknowledgement via on-call within 60 minutes.
  - Sev2: Acknowledge within 4 hours; engage within 8 hours.
- Escalation path: on-call SRE -> support manager -> TAM -> on-call engineering lead -> CTO on rare critical incidents. Escalations documented in the incident log (timestamped).

Incident comms templates and cadence:
- Initial customer notice: within 60 minutes of incident detection (template included).
- Status updates: every 60–90 minutes for ongoing Sev1 until mitigation, then 2× daily until RCA complete.
- Post-incident: preliminary RCA within 48 hours; full RCA and remediation plan within 10 business days for Sev1.

We should attach the sample webhook payload and the 'Initial Notice' template to the reply. I'll add the two small PDFs (notification workflow + templates).

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alan Reed <alan.reed@cedarbrook.com>, support_rfp@cedarbrook.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@redwood.com
Date: 2025-12-02T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFI - Support / TAM questions (Cedarbrook) — Redwood responses attached

Alan / Cedarbrook team —

Thanks for sending the RFI. Please find our consolidated responses below and attached as two files (Redwood_TAM_Coverage_Table.xlsx, Redwood_Incident_Notification_Workflow.pdf). Highlights: 

- TAM model: primary TAM + support pod. Standard TAM coverage is 9:00–17:00 local business hours (M–F). Enhanced TAM (contracted) provides 24/7 liaison with guaranteed TAM engagement within 60 minutes for Sev1.
- Support & incident SLAs: our support tiering and acknowledge/engage SLAs are in the attached workflow. Standard acknowledge for Sev1 is 30 minutes during business hours / 60 minutes outside. Enhanced support offers tighter SLAs and a contractual response clause.
- Notification channels: email, SMS, webhook, and Slack; webhook payload example included. We can integrate into Cedarbrook's incident management tool and deliver test webhook events during onboarding.
- Incident comms cadence: initial notice within 60 minutes, status updates every 60–90 minutes for Sev1, preliminary RCA within 48 hours, full RCA within 10 business days.
- Compliance evidence: SOC2 Type II report available under NDA; we will provide the summary and auditor contact upon request.

Next steps we propose:
1) If these answers fit your requirements, we'll send a one-page scope/pricing addendum for Enhanced TAM options.
2) We can schedule a 30-minute technical onboarding/demo of the notification webhook next week (suggest Wed 12/10 or Thu 12/11).

Attachements: Redwood_TAM_Coverage_Table.xlsx (xlsx, 1 sheet)
             Redwood_Incident_Notification_Workflow.pdf (pdf, 3 pages)

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Mina —

Thank you for the thorough and fast response. A couple quick clarifications before we move to procurement scoring:
1) For the Enhanced TAM 60-minute TAM engagement SLA — does that mean the TAM will be paged directly, or is that time measured from when Support first acknowledges the incident? We need clarity for contractual language.
2) For webhook delivery testing: can Redwood provide a short-lived sandbox endpoint we can test against, and a sample of the JSON body including severity and incident_id fields?

If you can answer those two items in a single email we can score you and proceed to commercial.

Best,
Alan

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alan Reed <alan.reed@cedarbrook.com>, support_rfp@cedarbrook.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@redwood.com
Date: 2025-12-02T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFI - Support / TAM questions (Cedarbrook) — quick clarifications

Alan — quick answers inline: 

1) Enhanced TAM 60-minute engagement: this refers to guaranteed TAM engagement (i.e., TAM will be paged and expected to be actively coordinating the incident) within 60 minutes of the incident being escalated to the TAM by Support. The contractual language we recommend: 
   "For Enhanced TAM, Redwood will page the assigned TAM and ensure TAM engagement (active coordination and communication with Cedarbrook stakeholders) within 60 minutes of Support escalation. Time measured from Support escalation timestamp in incident log."

2) Sandbox webhook and JSON sample: yes — we will provide a short-lived sandbox endpoint for Cedarbrook during onboarding and a sample JSON payload. Example (truncated):
{
  "incident_id": "RB-20251202-0001",
  "severity": "sev1",
  "status": "detected",
  "timestamp": "2025-12-02T14:58:12Z",
  "summary": "model-serving latency above threshold",
  "url": "https://status.redwood.com/incidents/RB-20251202-0001"
}

I can add that exact snippet to the workflow doc we already attached. Let me know if you prefer a demo of the webhook during the sandbox window.

Mina
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
